text: Outgoing emails must never tell customers that replies are automated or AI-generated (owner requirement, Nov 2026). A canned fallback email ('technical difficulties with our automated response system') was sent to a real customer when generation failed, and was removed. Rejected: rewriting the fallback as a neutral holding message, because it still sends a vague email on every failure and hides config errors. On failure the bot now sends nothing, retries, and records the email in failed_emails for a human to answer.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: Failure notifications go to ntfy (owner chose it over Telegram, Nov 2026). The owner wants only a generic 'support bot got an error' signal and explicitly does not want customer PII in it; the error text is a nice-to-have. Accepted tradeoff: the notification carries exception type plus text cut to 300 chars with the sender address redacted, although library exception text cannot be fully sanitized (code review flagged that it could in rare cases carry a subject). If customer data ever shows up in a notification, the agreed fallback is to send the exception type only. A --test-notification CLI flag existed for one commit and was removed: the bot runs unattended in Docker, so the owner preferred a 'Support bot started' notification on every start as the way to see that the channel works. Not built on purpose: Telegram, ntfy auth token, notifications for fatal startup errors, 'recovered' messages, shutdown message, a switch to turn the startup message off.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>
